h: A New Town with Ancient Neighbours
p: Livingston is one of Scotland's new towns, built from the 1960s onwards, and the Designer Outlet sits right in the heart of it. That makes it easy to combine bouncing with shopping, food and a visit to some of West Lothian's best spots.

Just a short drive north, Linlithgow Palace is the dramatic ruined palace where Mary, Queen of Scots, was born. It sits beside a loch, and the grounds, known as the Peel, are perfect for a walk and a picnic.

Nearby, Beecraigs Country Park, near Linlithgow, has woodland trails, a loch and a deer farm, plus play areas and outdoor activities. It's a great place to burn off any energy the trampolines didn't manage to.
On the shores of the Forth, Blackness Castle looks like a stone ship sailing into the water, and it's been used as a filming location for TV and film, which might win over older kids.

Further west, the Kelpies at Falkirk are two giant horse-head sculptures that are an amazing sight, and the Falkirk Wheel, a rotating boat lift linking two canals, is just a little further on. Both make for a cracking day out.
Livingston FC play at the Almondvale Stadium, close to the centre, so check fixtures if you're driving in on a Saturday.

With the M8 close at hand and train stations at Livingston North and Livingston South, it's an easy trip from Edinburgh, Glasgow and the towns in between, making it a handy halfway meeting point for families from both cities.
Plenty of free parking around the outlet helps keep the cost of the day down too.
